scope: Theorem 16.1 (Barrier and total trapped-region theorem) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 103. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (D, g, T) be smooth compact connected three-dimensional data with boundary Γ− ⊔ Γ+. Assume Γ+ ̸= ∅ and ΘT (Γ+) > 0 with its normal out of D. The inner boundary may be empty; when present it satisfies ΘT (Γ−) < 0 with its normal into D. All boundary parts may be disconnected. Consider all smooth bounding domains containing a relative collar of Γ−, avoiding Γ+, and having interior free boundary with ΘT ≤ 0 for the normal out of the bounding domain. If the union is nonempty, its closure is a maximal closed bounding region whose interior frontier is smooth, compact, embedded, stable, and satisfies ΘT = 0. It is itself the closure of an admissible domain. A nonempty strict inner barrier ensures a nonempty union and an enclosing stable MOTS. No energy condition or constraint equation is required for T.
